articles.title: 'Deep sense of insecurity': Sheikh Hasina flags minority safety in Bangladesh
articles.summary: Ousted Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina on Thursday expressed “deep concern” over a growing sense of insecurity among religious and ethnic
articles.body: Ousted Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina on Thursday expressed “deep concern” over a growing sense of insecurity among religious and ethnic minorities in the country, alleging continued attacks on minority communities, temples and homes since her ouster in August 2024.In her message on Sharadiya Durgotsav, Hasina, who is also the president of the Awami League, said this year's Durga Puja celebrations were taking place amid concerns over the safety of Hindus and other minority communities.She cited reports of killings, vandalism of idols, attacks on temples and homes, property seizures, extortion, violence against women and intimidation."But it is with deep sorrow and pain that I must say that this year's Durgotsav has come at a time when a deep sense of insecurity prevails among the religious and ethnic minorities of Bangladesh, including the followers of the Sanatan faith," Hasina said, according to news agency ANI."Since 5 August 2024, one incident after another of killings, persecution, vandalism of idols, attacks on temples and homes, seizure of property, extortion, violence against women and intimidation has continued to take place against minority communities across the country. This situation has become a cause of grave concern not only within the country but also internationally," she added.Her remarks come amid reports of attacks on Hindu places of worship and vandalism of idols and Durga Puja pandals during last year's festival, as well as wider concerns over reported violence against Hindus and other minorities since her government was ousted following a student-led uprising.Emphasising Bangladesh's history of communal harmony, Hasina said the country's founding ideals envisaged equal rights, dignity and security for people of all religious communities."Bangladesh is a land of communal harmony. The Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, dreamt of a Bangladesh where people of all religions and communities, including Hindus, Muslims, Buddhists and Christians, would live with equal rights, dignity and security," she said."Through the great Liberation War, we established Bangladesh on the basis of that very ideal. Our Constitution recognises secularism, equality, human dignity and the right of every citizen to practise their religion freely," she added.Reiterating her position on religious coexistence, Hasina said, "I have always said: religion belongs to each individual, but festivals belong to all. This country belongs to all of us."Hasina also accused the interim administration led by Muhammad Yunus of allowing an environment of impunity that, she alleged, had emboldened those responsible for violence against minorities, political opponents and ordinary citizens."By protecting the perpetrators instead of ensuring justice for the victims, the rule of law has been weakened and the perpetrators of violence have been emboldened. As a result, minorities, political opponents and even ordinary citizens have been plunged into fear and insecurity," she said.She further alleged that attacks on Awami League offices, businesses and properties had continued alongside arrests, politically motivated cases and the persecution of party leaders and supporters since August 2024.Raising concerns over the handling of cases involving alleged attacks on minority community members, Hasina questioned the lack of accountability and the treatment of those seeking protection for their communities."What kind of state system is this, where those accused of murder walk free, yet a religious leader remains in prison year after year for speaking about the rights and security of his own community?" she asked.She alleged that the lack of accountability had weakened public confidence in state institutions and added to the insecurity felt by minority communities.In her message, Hasina reiterated the Awami League's stated commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for minorities. She recalled that the party's 2024 election manifesto had promised to establish a National Minority Commission and enact a Minority Protection Act.She urged Awami League leaders, activists and supporters, along with citizens who believe in communal harmony, to stand with Hindu communities and avoid provocations."To my Sanatan brothers and sisters, I want to say: you are not alone. This country is yours too. Despite a hundred adversities, the people of Bangladesh have stood beside one another in each other's festivals for ages. No communal force will be able to sever that thousand-year-old bond or take away your right to this soil," she said.Hasina also said the message of good triumphing over evil, central to Durga Puja, remained relevant amid concerns over minority safety."Come, let us rebuild a Bangladesh where no one will be deprived because of their religious identity, where puja will not have to be performed with temples under guard, where a mother will not have to worry about her child's safety because of their religious identity, and where the state will give every citizen equal dignity and security," she said.She concluded by extending greetings to those celebrating Sharadiya Durgotsav and calling for a Bangladesh founded on peace, communal harmony, human dignity and equal rights.Separately, the Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council (BHBCUC) described the arrangements for this year's Durga Puja celebrations as “saddening and unfortunate”.In a statement, the council said the celebrations were taking place under tight security involving police, drones and political party leaders and activists.It said such arrangements were increasingly restricting the religious freedom of minority worshippers and damaging Bangladesh's image internationally, an outcome it said was undesirable.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'I'll forever celebrate you': Erika Kirk pens emotional tribute to late husband Charlie Kirk on his birthday - video
articles.summary: Erika Kirk, widow of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, paid an emotional tribute to her late husband on what would have been his 33rd birthday, sharing
articles.body: Erika Kirk, widow of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, paid an emotional tribute to her late husband on what would have been his 33rd birthday, sharing a compilation of videos celebrating his life and their relationship.“I thank God for your life,” Erika wrote in a post on X, reflecting on the years she spent with the Turning Point USA co-founder and the love they shared.“For the years He entrusted you to this earth… even though it didn’t deserve you. For the love that He allowed me to know so deeply as your wife,” she added.Erika recalled how Charlie made ordinary moments feel special and described their relationship as a once-in-a-lifetime love. She also shared a light-hearted memory of his fondness for mint chocolate chip ice cream.“I can’t even imagine how many scoops of mint chocolate chip ice cream you’re having in Heaven since calories don’t count up there, but down here, we’ll still save a scoop for you. Happy birthday baby,” she wrote.Charlie Kirk was 31 when he was fatally shot on September 10, 2025, during a campus event at Utah Valley University in Orem, Utah. The conservative activist was addressing students during a question-and-answer session when he was shot. Tyler Robinson has been accused of the killing.What Erika Kirk said after Charlie Kirk’s deathErika addressed the nation on September 12, 2025, two days after her husband's death, speaking about the personal loss and the impact on their two children.Recalling her return home after the shooting, she described how their three-year-old daughter ran into her arms and asked where her father was.Erika said she told her daughter that Charlie loved her deeply and was “on a work trip with Jesus so he can afford your blueberry budget”, referring to the family's expenses and her husband's love for their children.During the address, Erika also vowed to continue her husband's work and keep his legacy alive through the campus tour organised by Turning Point USA.“He never gave up. One of his mottos was never surrender. So I want to tell that we will never surrender,” she said.“The campus tour will continue. There will be even more tours in the years ahead to come,” she added.Erika also said her husband's ideas would continue to reach people despite his death, declaring that his voice would remain in a world filled with chaos, doubt and uncertainty.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Planned terrorist acts on behalf of Ukraine': Russia arrests Swedish man, charges him with illegal border crossing
articles.summary: Russia’s domestic intelligence agency, the FSB, on Thursday announced it has arrested a Swedish national, accusing him of plotting “terrorist attacks” and
articles.body: Russia’s domestic intelligence agency, the FSB, on Thursday announced it has arrested a Swedish national, accusing him of plotting “terrorist attacks” and “acts of sabotage” on behalf of Ukraine.According to the FSB, the 35-year-old has been charged with illegally crossing the border and could face additional terrorism-related charges.“Under the pretence of joining the ranks of the Russian Armed Forces, he travelled to the Russian Federation to carry out sabotage and terrorist acts at military facilities,” the agency said in a statement.The FSB also released a video of what it described as the man’s confession. Identifying himself as Freddy Lindholm from Stockholm, he claimed to have travelled to Russia to use FPV (first-person view) drones to carry out “terrorist attacks” and "acts of sabotage" on behalf of Ukraine.Speaking in English, Lindholm claimed that he had signed a contract with the Ukrainian army’s Aidar Battalion in the city of Ternopil before undergoing training in FPV drone operations for surveillance purposes. Russian state television also aired a copy of a contract he had purportedly signed with Ukraine’s defence ministry.Lindholm was arrested in Russia’s western Pskov region, near the borders with Latvia and Belarus.The FSB further stated that he had served as a Ukrainian drone commander under a contract from February to June, describing the unit as a “terrorist organisation”.Sweden’s foreign ministry acknowledged media reports about the detention but said it was not currently involved in the case. Ukraine had no immediate comment.Since the Russia-Ukraine war began in February 2022, Russian President Vladimir Putin has tasked the FSB with stepping up efforts to counter foreign spies and saboteurs.On Tuesday, the agency announced the detention of a Japanese journalist in Russia’s Far East on suspicion of espionage. articles.title: Police officer guilty of raping girl and woman in Shetland
articles.summary: Carmichael John Williamson was found guilty following a trial at the High Court in Edinburgh.
articles.body:
A police officer has been found guilty of raping a teenage girl and a woman in Shetland.

Carmichael John Williamson - known as John Williamson – was found to have engaged in sexual activity with a girl when she was under the age of 16 in 2014 and raped her between 2014 and 2015.

Williamson, of Burra, also raped a second woman in 2020 and again in 2022 when she was intoxicated and unable to consent.

The 32-year-old had denied the offences but was found guilty by a jury following a trial at the High Court in Edinburgh. He will be sentenced on 8 December.

Williamson cried in the dock after being told he would be remanded in custody when the verdict was delivered.

He was handcuffed and said "I love you" to his partner as he was led away.

Judge John Morris KC described it as an "anxious and distressing" trial.

Williamson was initially charged with nine offences, but five were dropped by the Crown before the closing speeches.

Jury sent home for night in trial of police officer accused of island rapes

Police officer tells rape trial he did not commit sex crimes

Williamson denied raping the teenager after she made contact through Snapchat when he was a student and he was himself a teenager.

He told the court the earliest time he could remember having sexual intercourse with the girl was the day after her 16th birthday.

He said allegations the sexual encounters happened when she was 15 were "untrue".

Williamson also denied taking part in sexual activity with an adult woman outside a community hall during an event in 2022.

He told the trial there was no further sexual activity with the woman later on at a house.

The court heard Williamson – a police constable for 10 years – was currently suspended by Police Scotland.

The force has been contacted for comment.

Williamson was placed on the sex offenders' register while sentencing was deferred so that reports could be obtained.

articles.title: Consumer court orders replacement or Rs 15 lakh refund after Force Motors vehicle developed engine defect within 2 months of purchase
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Karnataka has directed Force Motors and a dealer to replace a man's bus with a new vehicle of the same brand
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Karnataka has directed Force Motors and a dealer to replace a man's bus with a new vehicle of the same brand or refund Rs 15 lakh after finding an inherent manufacturing defect in the engine. The commission also ordered them to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.In its September 30, 2026, order, the commission found that the vehicle developed serious engine problems within months of purchase and that the dealer and the manufacturer failed to establish their defence that problems resulted from the driver's negligence.Why did the man approach the consumer commission?As per the commission order, Mugundappa, a driver by profession, purchased a Force Cityline passenger vehicle from authorised dealer Arihant Motors on April 2, 2024, for Rs 16 lakh. He alleged that he had taken loans to buy the vehicle and was supposed to earn a livelihood and support his family from the same.The vehicle came with a two year warranty. However, after driving it for around two months and covering about 9,000 km, the complainant faced engine overheating and seizure problems.He then took the vehicle to the dealer's service centre on May 27, 2024, and paid Rs 5,200. The problem recurred on June 10, 2024, when the coolant dried up and the engine seized again. Mugundappa had to tow the vehicle to the authorised service centre.The complainant further alleged that despite repairs, the vehicle could not run properly. He sought replacement of the vehicle or a refund of the purchase amount, along with interest, compensation and litigation costs.However, the dealer and manufacturer denied that the vehicle had an inherent manufacturing defect and instead argued that the driver had ignored the low coolant warning and used non-recommended coolant which caused the engine to overheat.They also claimed that the vehicle had been repaired under warranty and was ready for collection.What did the consumer commission find?The bench of President Sanjeev V Kulkarni and member S S Kadrollimath examined the evidence, including the complainant's documents and a mechanic's report, to understand whether the vehicle had a manufacturing defect or not.The commission observed that the complainant had faced problems soon after purchasing the vehicle and relied on the evidence of a mechanic who had examined it.“Considering the repeated major repairs and service rendered by OPs and considering the expert evidence of PW2 and Ex.P15/Report we hold that the complainant has proved that this purchased vehicle is having inherent manufacturing defect and as such the case made out by the complainant appears to be more probable and approximate and as such the evidence of PW1 and 2 is accepted on record, whereas OPs have failed to prove their defence. Hence complainant has made out case of inherent manufacturing defect crept in the newly purchased vehicle,” the commission noted.The bench further noted that the vehicle had been left at the dealer's showroom since June 10, 2024, and that the complainant had sought relief while the vehicle remained under warranty.“Hence we hold that, complainant has proved his case of deficiency in service and also proved that this passenger commercial vehicle is crept with major defect in the engine part and also gas kit and vehicle got seized on the middle of the road on 10.06.2024,” the commission added.The commission rejected the companies' defence and held that the vehicle had an inherent manufacturing defect. It also noted that the invoice established the purchase price as Rs 15 lakh, rather than the Rs 16 lakh claimed by the complainant.“Hence the purchased vehicle is having covered under warranty period and as such OP.1 and 2 shall bound to replace the vehicle by providing new vehicle of same brand of same price to complainant or in the alternative they shall refund invoice amount of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at 6 percent p.a., from 02.04.2024 till realization,” it further said.Final orderThe District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Belagavi, in its September 30, 2026, order, partly allowed the complaint and directed Arihant Motors and Force Motors, jointly and severally, to:Replace the vehicle with a new one of the same brand.Alternatively, refund Rs 15 lakh with 6 percent annual interest from April 2, 2024, until realisation.Pay Rs 10,000 as compensation for mental agony and suffering.Pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.The commission directed the companies to comply with the order within 45 days.

articles.title: Meet Holden Bierman, the 19-year-old Holly Springs, NC entrepreneur who started a beachwear brand at 12 with a $500 loan; six years later it is a six-figure business that says it helped remove 100,000 plastic bottles
articles.summary: Discover how 19-year-old Holden Bierman transformed a $500 loan into Coastal Cool, a six-figure sustainable beachwear brand that has removed over 100,000 plastic bottles from the ocean.
articles.body: Holden Bierman, an American teenager, built a swimwear brand at age 12 with a $500 loan from his parents. Started during the Covid-19 pandemic as a small clothing business, it has since grown into Coastal Cool, a sustainable beachwear company that says its products have helped fund efforts to remove plastic equivalent to more than 100,000 bottles from the ocean.The 19-year-old entrepreneur from Holly Springs, North Carolina, started by selling T-shirts and hoodies before shifting to swimwear made from recycled materials. Bierman launched his first business during the early days of the pandemic, when school closures left him looking for ways to spend his time.“I was just bored,” Bierman told Good Morning America. “Everybody was at home inside, nobody was outside, school was out. So I just started [to] research business ideas.”His interest soon developed into a business. Bierman officially launched Coastal Cool on his 13th birthday in August 2020, using the loan to pay for business registration, a website and sample products.How did Holden Bierman build his business?Bierman prepared a presentation for his parents explaining how he planned to use the $500. He then taught himself how to run an online business through YouTube tutorials, business podcasts and online forums.He learnt to build a website, source suppliers and ship products to customers. The business initially focused on casual clothing, but Bierman later decided to move towards swimwear.In an interview with The US Sun, Bierman said his interest in creating and selling products had started early. His father's work in sales and his mother's creative background also influenced his approach to business.“My dad gave me the business side, and my mom gave me the creative side,” he said.The move into swimwear helped Coastal Cool establish a clearer focus. Rather than selling only clothing, Bierman wanted to offer products that customers could buy while supporting an environmental cause.How does Coastal Cool help remove plastic waste?Coastal Cool makes swimwear using recycled materials, including polyester derived from discarded plastic bottles. The company also works with Tidey Ocean, a nonprofit that supports plastic collection and recycling and provides paid employment in communities affected by ocean pollution, according to its website.The partnership operates through a programme under which each product sold helps fund the collection and recycling of one pound of ocean-bound plastic.The company says its efforts have helped remove plastic equivalent to more than 100,000 bottles. The figure is based on the business's reported environmental impact.Bierman told Good Morning America that linking the brand to sustainability gave the business a broader purpose beyond selling products.The company also uses an on-demand production model, meaning products are made when customers place orders. This allows it to operate without holding large amounts of stock. Bierman has credited this approach, reinvesting profits and listening to customers with helping the business grow without outside investment.Balancing business and schoolHowever, managing the company alongside his education has required him to balance schoolwork with orders, social media and business partnerships. In interviews, Bierman has spoken about missing some typical high school events while working to expand the brand.His longer-term plans include taking Coastal Cool into more retail stores and studying a business-related subject at university.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ground temperatures at fire-ravaged Dunwich Heath still 53C
articles.summary: The National Trust says despite rainfall and cooler conditions, hotspots remain at Dunwich Heath.
articles.body:
The ground at a nature reserve that was ravaged during a huge wildfire in the summer is still recording high temperatures almost three months on.

Parts of Dunwich Heath and neighbouring RSPB Minsmere on the Suffolk coast were destroyed during the fire on 29 July , and it took the fire service nearly two weeks to stand down from the scene.

It was announced last month that the cause could not be determined . Many areas of the site still remain inaccessible as safety tests and monitoring tasks are carried out.

The National Trust, which owns and manages Dunwich Heath, said it was still recording temperatures of more than 53C in some areas, despite cooler temperatures and rainfall.

"While on site yesterday, Matt [Wilson], our countryside manager, recorded temperatures of over 53 degrees in some areas using a thermal imaging device," a National Trust spokesperson said.

"During the fire, earth-moving machinery was used to help crews tackle the flames, but the speed and scale needed at the time has meant vegetation such as gorse, heather and parts of trees have been churned into the banked soil and sand.

"In some places, this has created a charcoal kiln effect, which continue to retain heat even now."

The National Trust said that about seven weeks ago, it had recorded temperatures of about 65C on the heathland, at a time when ground heat averaged between 25C and 35C following prolonged hot weather in the summer.

However teams have reported seeing some fungi growing again in parts and even a common lizard has been spotted .

At the peak of the fire, 120 firefighters were at the scene, with all 35 of Suffolk's stations involved.

The fire ripped through an area the size of 210 football pitches and the fire service said the blaze had destroyed any potential evidence that might have identified the cause.

articles.title: Severe drought declared in parts of southern England
articles.summary: Reservoir levels continue to drop after a hot summer and less September rain than normal.
articles.body:
A severe drought has been declared across parts of southern England after months of low rainfall.

It was declared in parts of Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex and West Sussex.

The announcement by the Environment Agency follows a meeting of the National Drought Group, which reviewed water resources and drought conditions across England.

Supplies have been significantly impacted by high demand following the hottest summer on record.

The latest figures show Wimbleball Reservoir on Exmoor is at 14.9% capacity. Other major reservoirs are also low, including Roadford in Devon at 36.8%, Burrator at 33.6%, Colliford in Cornwall at 35% and Stithians at 21.9%.

The Environment Agency has classed Colliford and Wimbleball as having exceptionally low levels .

The government said customer water supplies would be uninterrupted.

Declaring a severe drought "ensures proactive steps are taken to safeguard water before any disruption occurs".
